message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for SHORT_LINE.

Opponent p2 has $225 cash. The current bid is $74. I will bid up to $99 and mortgage the property if I win.

If I drop out now, p2 wins for $74 and mortgages the property for $100, netting $26 in cash. That would be a loss for me. I must continue bidding up to $99.

p2's other railroads are mortgaged, so owning Short Line would only yield $25 in rent. The arbitrage is the real motivation.

I am on WATER_WORKS. p2's Orange and Dark Blue monopolies are lethal. St James, Tennessee, and New York each have four houses. Park Place and Boardwalk each have three houses. I need to see if my next roll lands on one of these properties.

I am checking whether p2 will land on my light blue properties. Standard Monopoly rent for Oriental Avenue with four houses is $450, and for Vermont Avenue with three houses it is $360.

Oriental with four houses pays $400. Vermont and Connecticut each pay $270 and $300. p2's Orange and Dark Blue monopolies are even more severe. St James, Tennessee, and New York each pay $750. Park Place pays $1100. Boardwalk pays $1400.

I have ten light blue houses. Selling them returns $250. Combined with my cash of $546 I have $796 in liquid assets.

States Avenue and Ventnor Avenue are unmortgaged with no houses. They can be mortgaged immediately for $70 and $130. Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut still have houses and cannot be mortgaged yet.

Total liquid assets are roughly $996, not the previously estimated $1156. Boardwalk at $1400 is impossible to survive. Park Place at $1100 is borderline. Orange and New York rents might be manageable if fully liquidated.

Bidding to $99 remains sound. Winning at that price or below nets positive cash after mortgaging. Forcing p2 to spend more of their $225 will make them more vulnerable to my light blue rent.

Bidding to $99 leaves p2 with only $126 after mortgaging, a net gain of just one dollar. This drains the arbitrage. Winning at $75 nets $25 cash instead. The mortgage value is zero above $100. I own Reading and Pennsylvania railroads, both mortgaged, so Short Line income is not needed.
